title: A token bucket refills when a request arrives

steps.title: Five tokens of burst capacity
steps.line: allow(now) adds refill on each call; no timer runs.
steps.caption: The bucket starts full at five tokens, and each accepted request spends one. allow(now) adds refill for the time since the last call, so no background timer runs. The chart will plot the balance over time; the dashed line is the one token a request needs.
steps.picture: Bucket balance: 5 tokens left, last refill at 0 seconds, 0 accepted; rejected requests: none; The bucket, filled to 5.0 of 5 tokens; A chart of tokens, 0 to 5, against time, 0 to 2.5 s, with a dashed line at the one token a request needs; Requests R1 to R10 at their arrival times: none answered yet; Code “bucket.allow(now), rate = 1”, 8 lines. Refill: 2: tokens = min(5; 3: tokens + (now - lastRefill) * rate); 4: lastRefill = now.

steps.title: Six at once: five 200s, then a 429
steps.line: No time passes, so no refill: R6 finds 0.0 tokens.
steps.caption: Six requests arrive at time zero. No time has passed, so refill adds nothing and the line drops one token per request. The sixth finds 0.0 tokens, under the dashed line, and gets 429.
steps.picture: Bucket balance: 0 tokens left, last refill at 0 seconds, 5 accepted; rejected requests: R6; The bucket, filled to 0.0 of 5 tokens; A chart of the balance over time: it climbs at 1 a second between calls and drops one token for each 200. Dots mark what R1–R6 found; R6 at 0.0 is under the one-token line and got 429; Requests R1 to R10 at their arrival times: 5 answered 200, R6 429, 4 waiting; Code “bucket.allow(now), rate = 1”, 8 lines. Refuse: 5: if (tokens < 1) return 429. New in this step: Bucket balance: 0 tokens left, last refill at 0 seconds, 5 accepted; rejected requests: R6; The bucket, filled to 0.0 of 5 tokens; A chart of the balance over time: it climbs at 1 a second between calls and drops one token for each 200. Dots mark what R1–R6 found; R6 at 0.0 is under the one-token line and got 429; and 1 more.

steps.title: Refill at 1/s: R7–R9 get 429, 200, 429
steps.line: Between calls the balance climbs 1 token a second.
steps.caption: Between calls the line climbs at 1 a second: (now − lastRefill) × 1. R7 at 0.5 s finds 0.5 and R8 at 1 s finds 1.0; R9 arrives at the same instant as R8 and finds what R8 left. R7 (0.5) and R9 (0.0) are under the dashed line, so they get 429.
steps.picture: Bucket balance: 0 tokens left, last refill at 1 seconds, 6 accepted; rejected requests: R6, R7, R9; The bucket, filled to 0.0 of 5 tokens; A chart of the balance over time: it climbs at 1 a second between calls and drops one token for each 200. Dots mark what R1–R9 found; R6 at 0.0, R7 at 0.5 and R9 at 0.0 are under the one-token line and got 429; Requests R1 to R10 at their arrival times: 6 answered 200, R6, R7 and R9 429, 1 waiting; Code “bucket.allow(now), rate = 1”, 8 lines. Refuse: 5: if (tokens < 1) return 429. New in this step: Bucket balance: 0 tokens left, last refill at 1 seconds, 6 accepted; rejected requests: R6, R7, R9; A chart of the balance over time: it climbs at 1 a second between calls and drops one token for each 200. Dots mark what R1–R9 found; R6 at 0.0, R7 at 0.5 and R9 at 0.0 are under the one-token line and got 429; Requests R1 to R10 at their arrival times: 6 answered 200, R6, R7 and R9 429, 1 waiting.

steps.title: R10 arrives at 2 s and gets 200
steps.line: R10 finds 1.0; min(5, …) keeps the balance at five or below.
steps.caption: R10 arrives at 2 s, one second after R9, and finds 1.0. The min(5, …) cap keeps the balance at five or below however long a client waits. R10 spends one token and leaves 0.0.
steps.picture: Bucket balance: 0 tokens left, last refill at 2 seconds, 7 accepted; rejected requests: R6, R7, R9; The bucket, filled to 0.0 of 5 tokens; A chart of the balance over time: it climbs at 1 a second between calls and drops one token for each 200. Dots mark what R1–R10 found; R6 at 0.0, R7 at 0.5 and R9 at 0.0 are under the one-token line and got 429; Requests R1 to R10 at their arrival times: 7 answered 200, R6, R7 and R9 429; Code “bucket.allow(now), rate = 1”, 8 lines. Spend: 6: tokens -= 1; 7: return 200. New in this step: Bucket balance: 0 tokens left, last refill at 2 seconds, 7 accepted; rejected requests: R6, R7, R9; A chart of the balance over time: it climbs at 1 a second between calls and drops one token for each 200. steps.title: The same ten requests at 1, 2 and 4 tokens a second
steps.line: 429s at 4 / s: R6; at 1 / s: R6, R7 and R9.
steps.caption: Each line is one run of allow() over the same ten requests, and the bright one is this case. A faster refill climbs back over one token sooner: at 4 tokens a second, R6 gets 429, and at 1 token a second, R6, R7 and R9 do.
